messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @oncall - realtime-p95 detector triggered for inference-main (p95 spiked > 2s for 3m). Alerts: grafana/r/realtime/p95, alert rule id 4092. Please acknowledge with /ack.
Anya: acked. I'm on it.
Samir: I'm seeing a correlated rise in streaming stall errors on the streaming ingestion path (conn.reset during chunk flush). p99 also climbed to ~5.2s.
Priya: @Anya can you confirm whether this is global or region-specific? Support reports a few customers in eu-west seeing degraded streaming sessions.
Anya: quick look — dashboard shows eu-west and us-west both affected, eu-east less so. Rolling p95 by region: eu-west 2.8s, us-west 2.3s, eu-east 1.1s.
Jordan: tails look noisy. I grabbed a flamegraph from the runtime for a stalled request: nvtx shows long wait on kv-cache fetch + lock contention inside the batching queue.
Samir: that matches logs: repeated "KV_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT" entries before stall. Example log: ``[2026-08-12T14:02:12Z] req=abcd1234 KV_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT model=redwood-7b-v2 seq=128``
Priya: customer-impact check: support says degraded for ~4% of active streaming sessions in affected regions (est. 1.6k sessions). Not all requests; mostly long-context chat streams.
Anya: immediate mitigations: 1) disable long-prefetch batching for streaming routes, 2) failover heavy requests to smaller kv-light model variant, 3) temporarily increase pool size for dedicated inference nodes. Which is fastest?
Jordan: fastest low-risk is toggling the batching policy to reduce max batch size for streaming endpoints. We can flip a runtime flag in the console within 60s.
Samir: failover to kv-light requires a routing policy change (route to redwood-7b-kvlight) — that also takes effect quickly because models are already warm in us-west, but eu-west might need warmup.
Elena: I can coordinate warming in eu-west if you want to route. Support: I'll prep a short customer note template if we need to notify enterprise tenants.
Priya: do we have an estimated cost impact for scaling pool? OpsBot: autoscale policy shows we can spin up +2 GPU nodes in eu-west within ~4m, cost delta ~$$/hr.
Anya: Plan: Jordan toggle batching -> observe 2 min -> if not improved, Samir flip routing to kv-light for streaming routes in us-west + eu-west (but warm eu-west first). Elena start customer comms draft. Priya will take on-call lead after initial handoff at +10m.
Jordan: toggled batching flag: ``/api/v1/runtime/configs/streaming?max_batch=8`` -> response 200. Watching p95.
Samir: seeing immediate drop in queue wait times in traces. p95 decreased from 2.7s to 1.6s in us-west within one minute.
Anya: eu-west improved but still >2s. Samir, please flip routing to kv-light in eu-west and kick a warmup job: ``POST /routing/switch {"from":"redwood-7b-v2","to":"redwood-7b-kvlight","route":"/v1/stream"}``
Samir: routing switch submitted. Warmup job started (20 warmup requests). Logs: ``warmup: model=redwood-7b-kvlight region=eu-west status=initiated``
oncall-bot: Incident note: page acknowledged by Anya at 2318004323. Incident severity: S2. Linking runbook: docs/runbooks/latency-streaming.
Jordan: after routing switch, eu-west p95 trending to 1.4s. Streaming stall errors dropped 85% across sampled requests.
Priya: taking over on-call in 10m. @Anya please handoff summary (what changed, what to watch).
Anya: handoff summary: - Cause: KV lookup timeouts under certain long-context streaming workloads + batching queue lockups. - Immediate mitigations: reduced streaming batch size (done), route heavy streams to kv-light in eu-west/us-west (done), warmup executed. - Monitoring: watch realtime/p95, streaming/stalls, kv-lookup-latency. - Customer impact: ~1.6k sessions, ~4% of active; major enterprise customers flagged by support: AcmeCorp, FinLens.
Elena: drafting customer note: "We detected elevated response times for streaming sessions in eu-west/us-west affecting a subset of sessions. We applied mitigations and will follow up with root cause analysis." Will post to support channel when you confirm.
Priya: thanks. I'll watch for regression and start incident page doc. Assigning follow-ups: - Samir to run root cause deeper analysis on KV backend (post-mortem 1) - Jordan to audit batching lock implementation and propose fix (post-mortem 2) - Anya to correlate rollout/traffic pattern changes around 14:00 UTC.
Samir: quick check: no anomalous infra events (no node reboots), KV backend error rate did spike; investigating slow GC / network hiccups between nodes.
OpsBot: autoscale completed: +2 nodes in eu-west at 2318004810.
Anya: p95 stable ~1.3s across regions now, p99 still a bit noisy ~3.1s but improving.
Priya: I'm officially on-call. I'll keep the channel open for 30m and then update incident doc with timeline and mitigation actions.
Samir: digging into traces now; will attach sample spans to the doc.
Elena: sent customer note draft to support channel for review.
oncall-bot: Reminder: if severity escalates to S1, run S1 protocol. For now severity S2.
Priya: thanks team. Next steps: keep monitoring for 15m. If p95 creeps >1.8s revert routing or increase capacity. I'll escalate if p99 >5s.
Anya: leaving channel, ping me if something spikes. :thumbsup:
